title: Conventional Comments Toolkit — repository configuration
description: Schema for .conventional-comments.json, read from a repository's default branch by conventional-comments-toolkit. Transcribed from packages/core/src/config/schema.ts; the validator in that file remains authoritative. Unknown keys are ignored with a warning at runtime — this schema flags them so you see them while editing.

$schema.description: URL of this schema. Editors use it for completion and validation.

version.description: Configuration schema version. A document declaring a version above the one a component supports is not applied: the component falls back to assist mode, or to the floor if the floor is stricter. Highest version supported today: 1.

mode.description: off — nothing happens. assist — the extension helps and diagnoses, the server publishes nothing. warn — same for the reviewer, but the server publishes a status that never fails, whose summary shows non-compliance. enforce — the check can fail and, if declared required, blocks the merge. Read the adoption guide before going past warn: enforce has five prerequisites.

formatSeverity.description: Whether comment format compliance (criterion 1) can fail the check. With "warn", a badly formed comment is reported but never blocks; only unresolved blocking threads do.

labels.description: Per-label overrides. Only the keys you list are overridden; every other label keeps its product default. Thirteen labels exist; ten are enabled by default.

id.description: Label identifier, always in English — it is a grammar token, not translatable text.

enabled.description: Whether the label may be used in this repository. typo, polish and quibble ship disabled.

blockingByDefault.description: Whether a comment carrying this label blocks when no decoration forces otherwise. True by default for issue, todo and chore.

alwaysNonBlocking.description: Whether the label can never block. A (blocking) decoration on such a label raises E-CONFLICT, and the verdict falls back to blockingByDefault.

icon.description: Emoji shown on the badge. Purely cosmetic: excluded from the configuration fingerprint, so it can never make two components disagree.

color.description: Badge border colour, conventionally #rrggbb. The validator only checks that this is a string, so the schema does not reject other forms either: a transcription that refuses what the product accepts is not a transcription. It only ever touches border-color, never a background at rest — so the applicable contrast criterion is WCAG 2.1 SC 1.4.11 (3:1 for a UI component boundary), not the 4.5:1 required of text. Cosmetic, and excluded from the fingerprint.

aliases.description: Alternative spellings accepted for this label, rewritten to the canonical form with a one-click fix.

decorations.description: The words allowed in parentheses after a label.

allowFree.description: Whether decorations outside the known list are accepted. They are rendered and counted, and never affect the verdict. Set false to raise E-UNKNOWN-DECORATION on anything unlisted.

known.description: Decorations whose effect on the verdict is defined.

forces.description: blocking — the comment blocks. non-blocking — it does not. null — no effect on the verdict; the decoration carries meaning for humans only.

severities.description: Re-level or silence individual diagnostics. Errors make a comment non-compliant; warnings are counted and shown, never a cause of failure. Codes not listed here keep their product severity, and an unrecognised code is accepted without complaint.

E-MALFORMED-PREFIX.description: A prefix that nearly parses, but does not.

E-UNKNOWN-LABEL.description: Label not enabled in this repository.

E-UNKNOWN-DECORATION.description: Unknown decoration while decorations.allowFree is false.

E-DECISION-SUBJECT.description: A decision reply shorter than rules.minDecisionSubjectLength.

W-CASE.description: Wrong casing. Ships a one-click fix.

W-DECORATION-STYLE.description: Spacing or ordering off. Ships a one-click fix.

W-SUBJECT-TOO-SHORT.description: Shorter than rules.minSubjectLength. Deliberately a warning at a low threshold.

W-MISSING-DECORATION.description: suggestion or question written with no decoration — the two labels whose blocking intent cannot be guessed.

W-NO-DISCUSSION.description: A blocking comment with no discussion under it.

W-NOT-BLOCKABLE.description: A blocking comment in a place that cannot carry that state.

scope.description: Which parts of a pull request are validated.

validateReplies.description: Whether replies inside a thread are validated. Even when false, a reply whose resolved label is decision is still read — otherwise the release valve would only work in repositories that had opted into validating replies.

validateReviewSummary.description: Whether a review's overall body is validated. An empty body is exempt regardless: an Approve with no text must never fail.

minSubjectLength.description: Below this, W-SUBJECT-TOO-SHORT. Deliberately a warning and a low threshold: making it blocking pushes people to work around the rule rather than apply it.

minDecisionSubjectLength.description: Minimum length of a decision reply, and the only length threshold that applies to it. Below it, E-DECISION-SUBJECT — an error, not a warning: closing a blocking point requires a sentence saying why.

exemptUsers.description: Authors whose comments are never validated, compared against the platform login, case-insensitively — never the display name.

allowlistPatterns.description: Regular expressions matched against the whole trimmed comment body. A match exempts the comment. Beyond the bounds this schema can express (50 patterns, 256 characters), an entry is also rejected at runtime if it is not a valid regular expression, or if it contains a nested quantifier — the shape behind most known ReDoS.

toolCommands.description: Comments addressed to a bot rather than to a human. EMPTY BY DEFAULT: slash commands used to be exempted through a built-in list, and that list is gone — in enforce mode a bare /rebase is now rejected like any other comment until the repository declares it here. Each entry is compared literally, never interpreted as a pattern.

oneOf.description: Sentinel enabling generic recognition of any slash command at the start of a body.
An exact bot handle. Matched on the whole first token, case-insensitively.

resolverOverrideGroup.description: The group whose members may override a resolution and record a decision. Designating it is a hard prerequisite for enforce: with an empty group both release valves are inert at once, and a blocking point whose author is unavailable holds the pull request with no recourse. Accepts a single group or a list.

overrideLabel.description: Name of the platform label that marks a pull request as exempt.

activatedAt.description: ISO 8601 instant from which pull requests are evaluated, or null for no cut-off. Anything Date.parse accepts is taken -- which is wider than RFC 3339, so no format is imposed here: "2026-09-01" is accepted at runtime and must be accepted in the editor too.

configUrl.description: URL of the organization configuration document. ONLY MEANINGFUL AT ORGANIZATION LEVEL: set in a repository file it is ignored and reported, because the organization URL comes exclusively from the floor channel.

coreMinVersion.description: Minimum core/ version required to apply this document. A component running an older major does not apply it: it falls back to assist mode, or to the floor if stricter. This — not the configuration fingerprint — is the lever for requiring a core/ version across an organization.

configCacheTtlSeconds.description: How long a resolved configuration is cached. A relaxation of mode does not wait for this: the organization document is probed separately and invalidates the whole cache as soon as a softer mode is observed.

badgeStyle.description: Badge shape. Two values are styled: "pill" and "flat". Any other string is accepted but renders unstyled. Cosmetic, and excluded from the configuration fingerprint.

shortcuts.description: Keyboard expansions in the comment editor.

abbreviations.description: Maps an abbreviation to the text it expands to. Defaults use as many letters as needed to be unambiguous: ?i, ?ib, ?ni, ?no, ?que, ?qui…

docUrl.description: Where the check's summary and the extension link for an explanation of the convention.

server.description: Server companion tuning. Ignored by the extension.

coalesceWindowSeconds.description: Window over which triggers for the same pull request are merged into one evaluation.

gracePeriodSeconds.description: How long the server keeps its last verdict when it cannot read the current state, before publishing a neutral grace-expired status.

reconcileIntervalSeconds.description: How often the server re-checks pull requests on its own. On Azure DevOps this must be 60 or below in enforce mode until an event channel is established, or the server emits a config-warning.

statusTargetUrl.description: Where the published status links. Required on platforms that render no status body.

exemptionLog.description: Where governed exemptions are recorded, so they are auditable rather than silent.

language.description: Language of descriptions and messages. Anything not starting with fr resolves to en. Label identifiers stay in English regardless — they are grammar tokens, not text.

telemetry.description: Disabled by default. No comment, code or diff content is ever sent, whatever this is set to.

severity.description: off — the diagnostic is not raised. warn — reported, never blocking. error — makes the comment non-compliant.
